title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten Emory spaces for quiet focus, group work, creative production, recreation, and community between classes.

cards.title: Settle Into the Matheson Reading Room
cards.subtitle: A high-ceilinged quiet room across the Level 3 bridge
cards.notes: Cross the Level 3 bridge from Woodruff Library, choose a large wooden table, and keep conversation for a group-study area.
cards.short_summary: Long tables, soft alcove seating, and a strict quiet expectation make this a focused reading destination.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory Libraries identifies the Matheson Reading Room as a designated quiet area with large wooden tables, chairs, sofas, and adjacent quiet rooms.
cards.source_title: Find a Quiet Study Area | Emory Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located on Level 3 across the bridge in Candler Library; users are asked to maintain utmost quiet.

cards.title: Build a Work Session Around the Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Flexible study and production resources across Woodruff Library
cards.notes: Start on Levels 1 or 2 for collaborative work, then use a reservable room or specialized workstation when the project calls for it.
cards.short_summary: This multi-floor commons combines ordinary seating with computers, study rooms, printing, and production tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory states that the Learning Commons provides multiple floors of study rooms, workstations, printing resources, and furniture for individual or collaborative study.
cards.source_title: Learning Commons in Woodruff Library | Emory University
cards.access_notes: Located inside Woodruff Library at 540 Asbury Circle; availability follows Woodruff Library building hours.

cards.entity_name: Marian K. Heilbrun Music and Media Library
cards.title: Work With Sound and Images at Heilbrun
cards.subtitle: A media-focused library on Woodruff Level 4
cards.notes: Bring a media assignment here for format playback or computer work, and use the open seating areas for quieter individual study.
cards.short_summary: Heilbrun pairs wooded views and quiet tables with playback stations, media collections, and adjacent creative software.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory Libraries says Heilbrun occupies Level 4 of Woodruff Library and offers media collections, 41 listening and viewing stations, computers, and MediaLab access.
cards.source_title: Marian K. Heilbrun Music and Media Library | Emory Libraries
cards.access_notes: Current Emory students, faculty, and staff may use its Learning Commons and MediaLab computers during business hours.

cards.title: Meet and Make on Cox Hall’s Second Floor
cards.subtitle: A technology lounge with workspaces and meeting rooms
cards.notes: Head upstairs from the food market, choose a workstation or lounge seat, and reserve a room when your group needs a defined workspace.
cards.short_summary: The second floor of Cox Hall supports both solo computer work and informal group meetups.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory describes Cox Hall’s second floor as home to lounges and the Computing Center, with computers, varied seating, and meeting rooms available to students.
cards.access_notes: Located on Cox Hall’s second floor; consult the linked Computing Center schedule because university holiday and activity hours vary.

cards.title: Take a Screen Break in the Rec Lounge
cards.subtitle: Games, billiards, and television on ESC South’s second floor
cards.notes: Drop in between classes for billiards or a video game, and check the RecRe lockers when your group needs controllers or board games.
cards.short_summary: This recreation lounge offers an indoor reset built around shared games rather than food or purchases.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory Student Center identifies the second-floor ESC South Rec Lounge as a place for pool, television, and video games, with games and controllers available through RecRe lockers.
cards.access_notes: Located on the second floor of Emory Student Center South; use is subject to student-center building access and event availability.

cards.title: Bring a Small Group to ESC North
cards.subtitle: A third-floor lounge with seating and screen mirroring
cards.notes: Use the third-floor seating for a casual meetup, and bring an HDMI-compatible device if your group wants to share material on a screen.
cards.short_summary: The North lounge is suited to low-key conversation and informal screen sharing between scheduled commitments.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory says the third-floor ESC North Lounge has comfortable seating and flat-screen televisions equipped with cable and HDMI screen-mirroring options.
cards.access_notes: Located on the third floor of Emory Student Center North; building access and lounge availability may change for events.

cards.title: Prototype an Idea at The Hatchery
cards.subtitle: Emory’s creativity and collaboration space at Emory Point
cards.notes: Bring an early-stage idea to the makerspace, use the available craft or fabrication tools, and ask staff about rooms for larger sessions.
cards.short_summary: The Hatchery gives student projects room to move from sketches and discussion into tangible prototypes.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory describes The Hatchery as a 15,000-square-foot creativity and collaboration space with an inclusive makerspace, classrooms, meeting rooms, and event space.
cards.access_notes: Located at 1578 Avenue Place, Suite 200; current posted hours vary between summer and fall/spring, and it is closed weekends.

cards.title: Find Collaborative Seating in the Science Commons
cards.subtitle: Atwood Chemistry Center’s central community hub
cards.notes: Use the varied seating for a study meetup near science classes, and move into one of the transparent meeting spaces when appropriate.
cards.short_summary: Atwood’s central commons mixes open seating, enclosed meeting areas, a library outpost, and a café.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory states that the Atwood Chemistry Center renovation created the Science Commons with meeting spaces, a library satellite, a coffee shop, and varied seating.
cards.source_title: Emerson Hall and the Atwood Chemistry Center
cards.access_notes: Located within the Atwood Chemistry Center; classroom, meeting-space, library, and café access may follow separate schedules.

cards.title: Choose a Quiet Table at Pitts
cards.subtitle: A theology library with public study areas and identity check-in
cards.notes: Bring focused reading rather than a video call, check in at the circulation desk, and follow the library’s no-food-and-drink policy.
cards.short_summary: Pitts offers a quieter academic setting with extensive collections and controlled but visitor-friendly entry.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitts states that it is an Emory professional library open to Emory patrons and checked-in visitors; its public spaces permit study but not online classes or calls.
cards.access_notes: Bring a valid Emory ID; visitors must show photo identification and check in. Online classes, calls, food, and drinks are not allowed.

cards.title: Shift to a Quieter Health Sciences Study Space
cards.subtitle: Individual and group study resources near Emory’s health schools
cards.notes: Use open seating for quiet work, or book an individual or group room when a health-sciences project needs privacy or collaboration.
cards.short_summary: This library broadens the study-space map beyond central campus with quieter seating and reservable rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory’s student academic toolkit lists Woodruff Health Sciences Center Library among quieter open-seating locations and among libraries offering study rooms to students.
cards.access_notes: Open seating and reservable rooms are separate options; check the library’s current access rules and reservation system before visiting.
